The two differ fundamentally: WikiLoop explicitly trains its knowledge-base construction on downstream feedback, while HippoRAG 2's knowledge graph is built offline with no downstream signal.

WikiLoop — downstream feedback drives construction. WikiLoop couples building and navigating an agent-native Wiki within a single role-conditioned policy, motivated by the observation that construction usually "receives no signal from downstream use" [2607.26604#s1.p1]. Its Builder reward is the marginal change in navigation utility: each patch is applied to an isolated copy and the frozen Navigator is run on both states, yielding ΔU_affected and ΔU_guard [2607.26604#s7.p8][2607.26604#s7.p12]. The reward is ΔU_affected minus a one-sided guard penalty for regressions on unrelated queries, plus edit-cost and structure penalties [2607.26604#s7.p14][2607.26604#s7.p17]. This guarded marginal-utility credit reduces guard regression from 0.046 to 0.016 (65.2% relative) while affected ΔAC stays near 12 [2607.26604#s12.p12]. The Navigator is also RL-trained on answer correctness, evidence recall, and cost [2607.26604#s6.p3].

HippoRAG 2 — no downstream feedback into the KB. HippoRAG 2 builds its graph offline: an LLM extracts schemaless OpenIE triples, synonym edges are added by embedding similarity, and passages become nodes linked by "contains" edges [2502.14802#s7.p4][2502.14802#s8.p2]. Retrieval uses query-to-triple matching, an LLM filter for recognition memory, and Personalized PageRank [2502.14802#s9.p1][2502.14802#s10.p1][2502.14802#s11.p1]. The page describes no training of the graph or retrieval from answer quality — the LLM components are used at inference, and the design is evaluated by recall@5 and F1 [2502.14802#s15.p1]. So the knowledge base is fixed and receives no feedback from downstream use.

In short, WikiLoop treats downstream navigation utility as the training signal for edits to its structured KB (with guard queries protecting unrelated content), whereas HippoRAG 2 constructs its graph once offline and never optimizes it against downstream outcomes.

Agent Zero Memory treats knowledge updates as versioned, provenance-bearing assertions rather than overwrites: it records each assertion with its origin, evidence, and calibrated belief, and its stated failure mode is that most systems "either overwrite silently or accrete contradictions" when a user corrects a fact [2608.29606#s1.p2]. Its design principle is citation-locked provenance — a provenanced item pairs content with origin, immutable timestamp, and evidence pointer, and an answer is only valid if every atomic claim is supported by an item the reader actually opened, otherwise the system returns ⊥, so fabrication is structurally excluded rather than discouraged [2608.29606#s6.p2][2608.29606#s6.p3][2608.29606#s6.p4]. Its three postulates are layering of raw sources/curated facts/inferred experience, provenance with calibrated belief under the citation lock, and grounded structure-aware retrieval by traversal [2608.29606#s6.p5].

Raw-RAG takes the opposite stance: it deliberately performs no knowledge update at all. It indexes source history without LLM-based extraction, summarization, graph construction, or mutation, keeping the original window text as reader evidence and leaving evidence interpretation and state reconstruction to the reader [2610.30755#s6.p1][2610.30755#s6.p2]. Its design principle is that naive dense-retrieval-plus-reranking over unprocessed history is a strong baseline — it ranks first in six of seven benchmark–model settings, and adding atomic-fact extraction, summary augmentation, or graph expansion reduces accuracy by 19.62, 5.81, and 5.78 points respectively [2610.30755#s1.p1][2610.30755#s12.p1]. It also achieves the highest evidence coverage (45.29% on MemoryAgentBench, 76.35% on MEME), which offsets less-than-best conditional utilization [2610.30755#s15.p7].

In short: Agent Zero Memory handles superseded facts by preserving them with provenance and enforcing citation-locked answers, emphasizing an honest, versioned model of what is known; Raw-RAG sidesteps supersession entirely by never mutating the store, emphasizing that raw, unprocessed retrieval is a strong and efficient baseline.

respuesta: In WiCER the CEGAR loop is reactive: the wiki is evaluated against diagnostic probes, and any probe scoring 1/5 triggers diagnosis of dropped facts that are fed back as preservation constraints—the document collection is the concrete system, the wiki the abstraction, a score-1 probe the counterexample, and pinning the refinement [2605.07068#s37.p1][2605.07068#s36.p1]. Online WiCER removes the static-corpus assumption and replaces this reactive probe-driven pinning with proactive pinning driven by a predicted materiality signal φ̂_t, adding decay-weighted eviction and periodic full recompilation every T_r steps [2606.09877#s2.p3][2606.09877#s31.p2]. Since queries arrive after the news batch, they cannot drive pinning; a bounded materiality signal φ_t(k,n)∈[0,1] acts as a query-relevance surrogate so facts are pinned before any query exposes a gap [2606.09877#s19.p2][2606.09877#s2.p3]. The key conceptual shift is formalized as predictive CEGAR: the counterexample becomes a predicted high-materiality news item rather than an observed QA failure, shifting refinement from diagnosis to prediction [2606.09877#s42.p1][2606.09877#s42.p4].

**TOKI (2606.06240):** It treats contradiction resolution in persistent memory as write-time concurrency control, casting the four production heuristics (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted merge, await-confirmation, per-rule policy) as bitemporal operators, each with an undeclared isolation precondition and admitted anomalies [2606.06240#s1.p1][2606.06240#s2.p1]. Each operator returns a winner with a system-time invalidation of the loser and emits an audit tuple [2606.06240#s10.p1]. Persistence is bitemporal: facts carry valid-time and system-time periods plus provenance and confidence [2606.06240#s6.p1], and a dual-row schema keeps current vs audit rows [2606.06240#s9.p1]. It names three LLM-specific anomalies — replay inconsistency N1, belief-drift skew N2, and audit erasure N3 [2606.06240#s11.p1] — and proves a guard map (RC/SI/SR) sound and tight [2606.06240#s11.p6][2606.06240#s12.p4].

**Relationship:** Both agree contradiction resolution cannot be separated from persistence semantics — 2604.11364 makes it a per-layer persistence requirement (supersession vs decay vs evidence-gated revision), while TOKI makes it a write-time isolation contract over bitemporal, audit-preserving storage. TOKI's audit-erasure anomaly (N3) and its supersession-with-invalidation mechanism align with 2604.11364's demand that knowledge be superseded with provenance rather than decayed [2606.06240#s11.p1][2604.11364#s8.p1].

respuesta: They differ in whether stale/conflicting memories are actively removed. HippoRAG (and HippoRAG 2) is an indexing/retrieval framework: it builds an LLM-extracted knowledge graph as a hippocampal index and retrieves via Personalized PageRank [2405.14831#s1.p1][2405.14831#s6.p4]; HippoRAG 2 adds passage nodes and LLM triple filtering [2502.14802#s7.p4][2502.14802#s10.p1]. Neither page describes a mechanism for detecting or resolving new/conflicting information—updates are simply added to the graph/corpus, and retrieval ranks by graph relevance, so old and new contradictory states can coexist and be retrieved together. GC-Mem, by contrast, is an inference-time consistency protocol aimed exactly at this: it formalizes Semantic Shadowing, where updated entity states leave old contradictory chunks in memory and dense retrieval returns the stale majority [2609.16073#s2.p2]. GC-Mem runs a pairwise NLI conflict oracle within the retrieved candidate set and applies a temporal dominance operator that excises any older chunk contradicted by a newer one, so the terminal state wins [2609.16073#s9.p2][2609.16073#s9.p4][2609.16073#s9.p5]. Thus HippoRAG handles new information by graph-based integration without explicit conflict resolution, while GC-Mem handles it by detecting contradictions and pruning superseded memories at query time [2609.16073#s1.p1].

respuesta: HippoRAG (and HippoRAG 2) do not address conflicting or superseded information at all: they are append-only graph indexes built offline from OpenIE triples plus synonym/passage edges, retrieved via Personalized PageRank, with no mechanism for detecting contradictions or removing stale states [2405.14831#s5.p2][2502.14802#s7.p4][2502.14802#s11.p1]. GC-Mem, by contrast, is an inference-time consistency protocol for mutable memory: it detects pairwise contradictions with an NLI oracle inside the retrieved candidate set and applies a temporal dominance operator that excises older contradictory chunks whenever a newer valid one is retrieved, so the new state wins [2609.16073#s1.p1][2609.16073#s9.p2][2609.16073#s9.p4]. This targets Semantic Shadowing, where stale but semantically equivalent chunks dominate dense retrieval and attention (the Majority Vote Trap) [2609.16073#s2.p2][2609.16073#s6.p4]. GC-Mem's effectiveness is bounded by conflict-detector recall, not precision [2609.16073#s16.p3][2609.16073#s20.p1].

respuesta:
HippoRAG handles new information by continuously updating its memory index rather than overwriting anything: new passages are processed by OpenIE into KG triples and merged into the existing knowledge graph, with synonym edges added by embedding similarity, so the index is "continuously updating" and supports knowledge integration across passages [2405.14831#s21.p1][2405.14831#s5.p2][2405.14831#s6.p1]. It has no explicit mechanism for detecting or resolving contradictions between old and new facts — retrieval just runs Personalized PageRank over the accumulated graph [2405.14831#s6.p4].

GC-Mem, by contrast, is built specifically for conflicting information. It treats entity state as piecewise-constant over transition timestamps, so the newest state is the only valid one and older contradictory states are contradictions [2609.16073#s5.p1][2609.16073#s5.p2]. Because stale and current chunks are semantically indistinguishable to the retriever, old states are not deleted and can dominate retrieval (Semantic Shadowing) [2609.16073#s2.p2]. GC-Mem therefore applies an inference-time temporal-dominance operator: a pairwise NLI conflict oracle runs within the retrieved candidate set, and any older chunk contradicted by a newer one is excised before generation [2609.16073#s9.p2][2609.16073#s9.p4][2609.16073#s9.p5]. This pruning is bounded by detector recall rather than precision [2609.16073#s16.p3][2609.16073#s20.p1].

In short: HippoRAG accumulates and integrates new knowledge into a graph index without explicit conflict resolution, whereas GC-Mem keeps history but resolves conflicts at query time by pruning temporally dominated contradictory chunks [2405.14831#s21.p1][2609.16073#s1.p1].
